storymap_section: 1. Title / hero and 5. Global discovery screen
recommended_display_size: Cover image crop if legible; otherwise full-width image after opening text
caption: Filtered positive residual culinary corridors after a geographic distance baseline. Blue links highlight the East/Southeast Asia focused case; orange links show global discovery candidates. Line width represents residual strength. The figure shows where food similarity exceeds distance-based expectation; it does not identify historical causes.
alt_text: A world map with colored lines connecting cuisine anchor locations. Blue lines emphasize East and Southeast Asian cuisine links, while orange lines mark other positive residual cuisine links discovered by the global screen.
source_method_note: Run 4 revised figure from filtered Run 2 v2 residual corridor outputs and cuisine coordinate crosswalk.
limitation_note: Discovery layer only; not proof of global culinary causality or representativeness.

recommended_display_size: Full-width image; enable expand image if available
caption: Cuisine similarity plotted against log geographic distance. The fitted trend is the distance baseline. Points above the trend have positive residuals and become candidate culinary corridors. This figure makes the core GIS operation visible: comparing food similarity to spatial expectation.
alt_text: A scatter plot showing cuisine-pair ingredient similarity against geographic distance, with a fitted downward trend line. Points above the trend are interpreted as positive residual culinary corridors.
source_method_note: Run 4 revised figure from filtered cuisine similarity and pairwise distance model outputs.
limitation_note: A distance model explains association, not cause; residuals are candidates for interpretation.

recommended_display_size: Full-width image or sidecar media panel
caption: East/Southeast Asia focused case using filtered positive residual cuisine links. Thicker blue links indicate stronger residual similarity after the distance baseline. This is the strongest inference case because it is spatially coherent and avoids relying on the full global network for interpretation.
alt_text: A regional map of East and Southeast Asia showing cuisine anchor points connected by blue residual links, including Chinese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, and Filipino cuisine relationships.
source_method_note: Run 4 revised focused-case figure from Run 2 v2 focus-case outputs.
limitation_note: Focused inference case; still not proof of a specific historical mechanism.

recommended_display_size: Full-width image; enable expand image; place immediately after East/Southeast Asia case
caption: East/Southeast Asia residual cuisine links over shaded relief and coastal context. The map makes the focused corridor visually legible by placing residual links near coastlines, islands, peninsulas, relief, and maritime space. It is a relief-context map, not a measured least-cost route or causal terrain model.
alt_text: A shaded-relief map of East and Southeast Asia with residual cuisine links drawn across mainland and maritime contexts, highlighting Thai-Vietnamese, Chinese-Korean, and Filipino-related links.
source_method_note: Run 5 figure using Run 4 v2 East/Southeast Asia residual/accessibility metrics, cuisine coordinates, and local Basemap ETOPO-style relief image.
limitation_note: Spatial context only; does not prove topography, maritime routes, migration, or trade caused the similarities.

recommended_display_size: Full-width image; emphasize as key Fisher contribution
caption: Residual bridge index by cuisine. The index aggregates positive residual degree, top-residual participation, mean positive residual strength, long-distance residual score, and mean residual into mapped place-level roles. This cannot be derived from ingredient vectors alone because it depends on geographic distance and the spatial residual network.
alt_text: A map or chart showing cuisines as place-level nodes with bridge-index values, identifying which cuisine anchors participate in multiple unexpectedly strong residual links.
source_method_note: Run 4 geospatial upgrade using filtered residual corridor outputs and coordinate anchors.
limitation_note: Bridge roles describe residual-network position; they do not identify causal pathways.

recommended_display_size: Full-width image or appendix-style body image
caption: Boundary/permeability diagnostic summarizing mean residual similarity by spatial grouping. Positive values indicate that similarity is higher than distance-only expectation on average. The result supports spatial structure while remaining diagnostic rather than causal.
alt_text: A diagnostic figure comparing residual cuisine similarity across spatial groupings such as same subregion, cross-subregion, and secondary corridor classes.
source_method_note: Run 4 revised figure from Run 2 v2 boundary/permeability summaries.
limitation_note: Diagnostic figure; use to show sensitivity and caution, not as primary proof.

storymap_section: 7. Topographic corridor context, optional sidecar or appendix
recommended_display_size: Sidecar side panel or optional appendix image if layout has room
caption: Corridor callouts showing two focused residual situations: Thai-Vietnamese mainland adjacency and Filipino links in a maritime/island setting. The callouts clarify spatial contexts that are harder to see in the full regional relief map.
alt_text: Two zoomed map panels: one highlighting a mainland residual link between Thai and Vietnamese cuisine anchors, and another highlighting Filipino residual links in an island and maritime context.
source_method_note: Run 5 callout figure using the same residual/accessibility metrics, coordinates, and relief background as the primary Run 5 map.
limitation_note: Optional contextual zoom; not necessary if the main topographic corridor map is clear.
